title: Novel Hsp90alpha inhibitor inhibits HSV-1 infection by suppressing the Akt/beta-catenin pathway.
authors: Wang, Zexu; Zou, Weixiangmin; Zeng, Qiongzhen; Song, Xiaowei; Li, Menghe; Pang, Jiaping; Zhu, Hai; La, Caiwenjie; Wang, Xiao; Wang, Yifei; Zheng, Kai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Hsp90alpha抑制剂JD-13抗HSV-1感染，涉及分子对接与MD模拟但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The prevalence of herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) infection and the emergence of drug-resistant HSV-1 strains posts a significant global health challenge, necessitating the urgent development of effective anti-HSV-1 drugs. As one of the most prevalent molecular chaperones, heat shock protein 90 alpha (Hsp90alpha) has been extensively demonstrated to regulate a range of viral infections, thus representing a promising antiviral target. In this study, we identified JD-13 as a novel Hsp90alpha inhibitor and explored its capability in inhibiting HSV-1 infection. METHODS: The inhibitory effect of JD-13 on Hsp90alpha activity was confirmed by molecular docking, molecular dynamic stimulations, fluorescence quench titration and cellular thermal shift assay. The antiviral activity of JD-13 was examined by viral plaque assay, RT-qPCR, Western blot, flow cytometry, fluorescence microscopy and time-of-addition assay. The in vivo antiviral efficacy of JD-13 was evaluated in the HSV-1 skin infection guinea pig model by analyzing skin lesions and herpes formation. RESULTS: JD-13 significantly inhibited the infection of both normal and acyclovir-resistant HSV-1 strains. In addition, JD-13 alleviated skin damage in guinea pigs caused by cutaneous HSV-1 infection. Further studies revealed that JD-13 impaired HSV-1 early infection and suppressed the Akt/beta-catenin signalling pathway by promoting Akt degradation. Consequently, the inhibition of the Akt/beta-catenin signalling pathway restricted HSV-1 infection. CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest JD-13 as a novel HSP90alpha inhibitor with the potential to be developed as an antiviral agent for the treatment of HSV-1-related diseases.
abstract_zh: 目的：1型单纯疱疹病毒（HSV-1）感染的普遍性及耐药性HSV-1株的出现构成了重大的全球健康挑战，亟需开发有效的抗HSV-1药物。作为最普遍的分子伴侣之一，热休克蛋白90α（Hsp90alpha）已被广泛证明可调控多种病毒感染，因此是一个有前景的抗病毒靶点。在本研究中，我们鉴定JD-13为一种新型Hsp90alpha抑制剂，并探讨其抑制HSV-1感染的能力。方法：通过分子对接、分子动力学模拟、荧光猝灭滴定和细胞热位移实验确认JD-13对Hsp90alpha活性的抑制作用。通过病毒噬斑实验、RT-qPCR、Western blot、流式细胞术、荧光显微镜和加药时间实验检测JD-13的抗病毒活性。在HSV-1皮肤感染豚鼠模型中，通过分析皮肤病变和疱疹形成评估JD-13的体内抗病毒疗效。结果：JD-13显著抑制正常和耐阿昔洛韦HSV-1株的感染。此外，JD-13减轻了豚鼠皮肤HSV-1感染引起的皮肤损伤。进一步研究表明，JD-13通过促进Akt降解，损害HSV-1早期感染并抑制Akt/β-catenin信号通路。因此，Akt/β-catenin信号通路的抑制限制了HSV-1感染。结论：这些结果表明JD-13是一种新型HSP90alpha抑制剂，有潜力被开发为治疗HSV-1相关疾病的抗病毒药物。
